owner: FileSteward cross-domain ownership and necessity classification
purpose: Determine what storage belongs to, what currently depends on it, and whether it is active, legacy-candidate, regenerable, shared, or unresolved before FileSteward asks the operator for a keep/remove preference.
core_rule: A filesystem path may have multiple owners and dependency edges. No single source (path, age, Entire, Git, registry, package manager, process list, or model confidence) may alone authorize deletion.

adapters: HKLM/HKCU uninstall entries in both registry views
ahead/behind or push equivalence when available

entire_cli.authority: context accelerator and repository relationship/activity evidence; never deletion authority
graph_when_available: entire graph query/explain/neighbors/impact against working tree for current dependency relationships
entire graph query/explain/neighbors/impact --head when committed-tree comparison is required
entire graph snapshot/symbols/edges only when bulk graph evidence is materially useful
required_interpretation: working-tree graph evidence may prove current code relationships and change impact
HEAD graph evidence may distinguish committed baseline from uncommitted current work
Entire session/checkpoint/context evidence may increase activity confidence but cannot by itself make a repo or file legacy
absence from Entire evidence is never proof of dispensability

examples: toolchain/runtime dependency from another active project

REPO_STABLE.meaning: clean and reproducible but still intentionally present; not legacy merely because inactive

required_all: no unpushed commits or unresolved branch uniqueness
no current Entire session/change-impact evidence when Entire is available
no cross-repo dependency edge requiring local presence

REPO_GENERATED_OUTPUT.meaning: build/cache/generated bytes whose source boundary and deterministic recreation are proven

APP_ACTIVE_REQUIRED.meaning: installed/runtime/serviceability evidence binds the storage to an application the system currently recognizes

APP_BROKEN_REQUIRED.meaning: application remains registered/expected but a required install/serviceability component is missing

APP_CACHE_REGENERABLE.meaning: application-owned cache boundary with deterministic regeneration proof

APP_ORPHAN_CANDIDATE.meaning: no surviving owner/dependency found after all safe app attribution adapters; absence of evidence alone is not deletion proof

examples: repo file also used by an installed app => preserve until both repo and app dependency are resolved
toolchain cache shared by multiple repos => semantic cache cleanup only after shared dependency/recovery proof
generated output inside active repo => may be reclaimable only if generation boundary is proven and repo state remains protected

must_show: why FileSteward thinks the item is active/stable/legacy-candidate/regenerable
evidence confidence/provenance without asking the user to interpret raw technical output
user_facing_projection.rule: Classification describes evidence and consequence, not a deletion recommendation. The operator chooses value/preference only after technical safety is machine-resolved.

deletion_gate.requires: current cross-domain ownership graph revision bound to manifest/preflight and rechecked immediately before each mutation
